mmImgszRow.detection_resolution_the_engi: Detection resolution the engine is built for - a multiple of 32 (YOLO stride). Higher (e.g. 960) downscales the frame less, so small or faint mosaics detect better, at the cost of slower compile and detection and more VRAM. 640 is the tested default; 960 suits dense VR content.

ctrlCodec.title: Output codec. AV1 needs an RTX 40-series (Ada) or newer to ENCODE (30-series can only decode it); ~30% smaller files than HEVC at the same quality, and previews play in the app without any HEVC extensions.
sectEncoder.constant_quantization_parame: Constant quantization parameter. Lower = higher quality, larger file (0-51)
sectEncoder.encode_on_a_background.title: Encode on a background thread, overlapping NVENC with detection/restoration — up to ~20-25% faster on encode-heavy runs. Needs VRAM headroom (adds a ~500-600 MB frame queue at 4K) and can hit NVENC errors on saturated or low-VRAM cards. Leave OFF unless your card has room to spare.
sectEncoder.nvenc_speed_quality_preset.t: NVENC speed/quality preset. P1 fastest … P7 best quality
sectEncoder.where_the_per_run.title: Where the per-run files go: the run report (.run.json), its console log (.log) and the timecodes file (.timecodes.txt). Beside the video = next to the output (default); Temp folder = in the Temp folder; Off = not written at all. The app's own console log in the program folder is not affected.
sectMaskPreview.add_mosaic_sfw_censor.ti: Add Mosaic (SFW censor): instead of restoring, PIXELATE each detected region. Uses the selected Detection model (e.g. the NSFW model); no restoration model needed. Test Frame, Restore and Restore & Save all run in this mode — output is saved as -censored.mp4. Mutually exclusive with Preview Detection.
sectMaskPreview.fast_coverage_check_inst: Fast coverage check: instead of restoring, fills each detected region with a flat colour (set below) so you can see exactly what the detector found - without waiting for restoration. Any mosaic still visible is a detection miss; adjust Score or Image Size. Mutually exclusive with Add Mosaic.
sectMaskPreview.flat_fill_colour_for.tit: Flat fill colour for detected regions
sectMaskPreview.mosaic_cell_size_in.titl: Mosaic cell size in pixels for Add Mosaic mode (bigger = coarser blocks).
sectMosaicDetection.detector_input_resol: Detector input resolution (multiple of 32). Higher (e.g. 960) downscales the frame less, so small or faint mosaics detect better, at the cost of slower detection and more VRAM. 640 is the tested default; 960 suits dense VR content. With Use Tensor on, the compiled engine must match this size - if it doesn't, the run falls back to PyTorch at this size and the log tells you to recompile at the new size in Manage Models.
For VR studios that apply the mosaic in VIEWING space: blocks look square in the headset but arrive warped in the raw frame, which detection and restoration handle poorly. Fisheye warps each eye so those blocks become square again, analyzes there, and warps only the restored regions back - background pixels are never resampled. Leave Off for content whose mosaic already looks square in the flat player (most studios). Requires Split SBS.
sectMosaicDetection.how_confident_the_de: How confident the detector must be to accept a mosaic (0.05-1.00). Lower catches more, including faint or partial mosaics, but risks false positives on mosaic-like texture; higher is stricter. Start around 0.25 and lower it if mosaics are being missed.
How many frames the detector processes per GPU call (1-16). Higher is faster but uses more VRAM - lower it if detection runs out of memory. Affects only speed and memory, not quality.
Side-by-side stereo (VR): split each eye, detect separately, merge, and keep restorations from crossing the seam.
sectMosaicDetection.use_fp16_precision_f: Use FP16 precision for detection (selects the fp16 detection engine)
sectMosaicDetection.use_the_compiled_ten: Use the compiled TensorRT engine for detection if available (faster). Unchecked = PyTorch .pt.
sectMosaicDetection.when_two_detections_: When two detections overlap, how much overlap is allowed before they are merged into one (NMS). Lower merges more aggressively into fewer, larger boxes; higher keeps more separate boxes. Rarely needs changing from ~0.70.
sectMosaicRestoration.blend_the_restored: Blend the restored patch using the detector exact pixel outline of the mosaic (segmentation mask) instead of its rectangular box. On = cleaner edges that follow the mosaic real shape; off = the whole box is blended. Leave on unless the mask looks wrong.
sectMosaicRestoration.extra_cleanup_pass: Extra cleanup pass on upscaled regions (RTX Super-Res modes only; Real-ESRGAN is unaffected). Chains a second Maxine pass in DENOISE mode after the upscale, so pasted regions come back cleaner - most visible on large regions and in VR viewing. Loads a second Maxine effect (extra VRAM) - on 6 GB cards weigh it against the run's headroom. Approach ported from jasna (AGPL), with credit.
sectMosaicRestoration.grow_every_detecte: Grow every detected region outward by N pixels before restoring (0-64). Helps when the detector box is slightly tight and leaves a mosaic rim - a few pixels covers the edge. Too much wastes work and can touch clean areas. 0 = off.
sectMosaicRestoration.how_many_consecuti: How many consecutive frames the restorer processes together as one clip - this IS the model's temporal window, so longer clips give smoother, more stable motion but use more VRAM. As of v1.60 engines are clip-size independent: with Use Tensor on the dial is free up to 720 on one compiled set (past ~180, wall time stops improving and only memory grows). With Use Tensor off (PyTorch) the dial is free up to 600. On both paths the only ceiling is memory - a too-long clip stops with a clean out-of-memory error; dial down and retry (the restoreChunkFrames config entry can also cap the PyTorch window without shortening clips). Independent of detection.
sectMosaicRestoration.how_the_restored_p: How the restored patch is blended back into the frame. None = a rectangular blended region (can leave a hard ice-block edge around the mosaic). Face Swap = the blend follows the mosaic actual shape with a soft inward edge, reducing that rectangle - usually cleaner, especially on SBS/VR content. (Blending scheme adapted from Rope's face-swap compositor.)
sectMosaicRestoration.sharpens_large_res: Sharpens large restored regions. Restoration works on a 256-px crop; regions bigger than that get stretched at paste-back and look soft - worst on VR close-ups. A secondary scaler upscales the restored crop 2x or 4x with real super-resolution first, so paste-back shrinks instead of stretching. Regions smaller than 256 px are untouched. RTX Super-Res (NVIDIA Maxine) needs an RTX GPU and a recent driver and uses about 1.5 GB extra VRAM. Real-ESRGAN (bundled model, no downloads) works on every GPU - NVIDIA, Intel Arc, and AMD. Applies only to real restoration (not Preview/Add Mosaic). If unavailable the run continues without it and says so in the log.
sectMosaicRestoration.smooths_per_frame_: Smooths per-frame restoration/upscale shimmer (fizzle, wiggly fine detail) by averaging each restored frame with its 6 temporal neighbors where the content agrees - real motion and lighting changes pass through untouched. Runs on restored regions only; the rest of the frame is never modified. Uses the vs_temporalfix model (tiny, ~2 MB); needs its .pth weights next to the restoration model or in models/. Higher strength = more aggressive smoothing; too high may soften very small movements. Real restoration only.
sectMosaicRestoration.soften_the_edge_wh: Soften the edge where the restored patch meets the original frame by N pixels (0-64). Higher hides the seam for a smoother blend; 0 = auto. Applies when Blend Mask = Face Swap (the shape-aware edge). With Blend Mask = None it has no effect.
sectMosaicRestoration.use_fp16_precision: Use FP16 precision for restoration (selects the fp16 engine set)
sectMosaicRestoration.use_tensorrt_engin: Use TensorRT engines for restoration (much faster). Unchecked = PyTorch. Needs compiled sub-engines for this model + precision + clip size.
sectMosaicRestoration.where_decoded_fram: Where decoded frames wait for paste-back. Auto (recommended): on NVIDIA, Re-decode -- no frame store at all; a second decoder produces each frame again when it is due, so Max Clip Length costs no RAM or VRAM and no full frame crosses the PCIe bus. On AMD/Intel, Auto keeps the frame store: GPU VRAM when it fits, system RAM when it would not. Device forces VRAM (the classic behavior); Host forces system RAM; Re-decode forces the second decoder (NVIDIA; Split SBS yes, VR Projection and Test Frame keep the store).
